name: Breitenwang
kurzbeschreibung: Neighboring municipality of Reutte with Plansee and the famous golf course.
beschreibung:
Overview

Breitenwang is a historic municipality in the Außerfern region of Tyrol within the Reutte district, located at approximately 850 meters above sea level in the Reutte valley basin. Home to around 1,500 residents, the village directly borders the district capital of Reutte while maintaining its distinct rural identity and prominent cultural legacy as the historic mother parish of the Außerfern. The municipal area of nearly nineteen square kilometers extends from the valley floor across the forested slopes of the Ammergau Alps up to the fjord-like shores of Lake Plansee and the Bavarian border, marrying celebrated sacred art with pristine alpine landscapes.

History

The settlement was first documented in 1094 as Breitinwanc, meaning broad meadow, when Welf Duke Welf IV donated local estates to Weingarten Abbey. An epochal moment in European history occurred in December 1137: returning from his coronation campaign in Rome, Holy Roman Emperor Lothar III fell gravely ill and died in Breitenwang on December 3/4, 1137, in a modest shelter. In accordance with the medieval custom of Mos Teutonicus, his body was prepared for transport back to Königslutter; a bronze plaque on the church steeple commemorates his death. For centuries, Breitenwang served as the ecclesiastical mother parish for the entire Außerfern region, encompassing Reutte and the Lech Valley. Adjacent to the Deanery Church of Saints Peter and Paul, the Resurrection Chapel houses a celebrated Baroque Dance of Death created between 1724 and 1728 by plasterer Thomas Seitz: ten stucco medallions depict Death leading representatives of all social estates, representing a rare artistic treasure of the German-speaking world.

How to Get There

By car, visitors reach Breitenwang toll- and vignette-free from Germany via motorway A7 through Füssen and the border tunnel along the Fernpass federal highway B179, taking the Reutte-Nord or Süd exit. From Innsbruck, access leads across the Fern Pass on the B179. From the village center, provincial road L255 leads directly to Lake Plansee and onward to Linderhof Palace in Bavaria. Rail travelers take the Außerfern Railway to Reutte in Tirol station, located just one kilometer from Breitenwang.

Tips

An absolute highlight is Lake Plansee, Tyrol's second-largest natural lake, renowned for drinking-water clarity, passenger boat cruises aboard MS Margarethe, sailing, and alpine scuba diving. A thrilling outdoor hike leads through the Stuibenfälle waterfalls along the Archbach stream, featuring the secured Hermannsteig path and a scenic suspension bridge over thundering cascades. Cultural travelers should visit Saints Peter and Paul Church with its Rococo frescoes by Johann Jakob Zeiler and the famous stucco Dance of Death. The nearby Alpentherme Ehrenberg spa complex and the Ehrenberg Castle ensemble with the highline179 pedestrian suspension bridge complete an extraordinary visitor experience.
